spectrum.note: How sudamp draws the classic spectrum (Sources/SkinKit/Render/Visualizer.swift, VisualizerRenderer.draw, after Webamp's Vis.tsx/VisPainter.ts). In the 76x16 visualiser rect: fill with viscolors[0]; put a viscolors[1] grid dot at every even x (0, 2, ..., 74) on every odd y (1, 3, ..., 15). Then for bar i = 0...18 (low to high frequency) at x = 4i, 3 px wide with a 1 px gap (column 75 stays background): the bar fills its bottom h rows, h = round(value * 16) for value 0...1, and screen row r (0 = top, 15 = bottom) is always viscolors[2 + r] - the gradient belongs to the rows, so a short bar shows only the bottom colours. Then if the peak p = round(peak * 16) > 0, a 3 px line at row 16 - p in viscolors[23], drawn over the bar (it replaces the bar's top row when p = h). Bars and peaks are drawn over the grid dots. Redrawn at 30 Hz. Same rect and rule for every skin; only the 24 colours change.

rect.source: MainLayout.visualizer, Sources/SkinKit/Render/Layout.swift; composited there by SkinPicture.composite, Sources/Shell/AppSnapshot.swift

spectrum.gridDots: even x, odd y, relative to the rect
spectrum.peakRow: 16 - round(peak * 16); no peak when that rounds to 0
spectrum.falloff: Bars rise at once and fall 0.75 rows per 30 Hz frame (Winamp 'moderate', 1.40625 full heights a second). A peak jumps up with its bar, then falls, starting at 3/256 row per frame and 1.1 times faster every frame (Sources/Audio/VisualiserAnalyser.swift Settings, after Webamp's VisPainter.ts). Without analyser peaks, SkinUI's PeakTracker holds a peak 8 frames, then drops it 0.5 rows a frame.
spectrum.analyser: 19 log-spaced bands, 40 Hz-16 kHz, from a 1024-sample Hann-windowed DFT at 48 kHz; -60 dB is an empty bar, -6 dB (re a full-scale sine) a full one.
spectrum.oscilloscope: 76 samples -1...1, one per column; row = round((1 - (s + 1) / 2) * 15); each column joined vertically to the previous sample's row; colour viscolors[18 + k] with k = 0 on rows 6-7, 1 on 4-5 and 8-9, 2 on 2-3 and 10-11, 3 on 0-1 and 12-13, 4 on 14-15.
